Details: Communist organizers build national pressure while contesting control of individual states. The root event immediately seeds one Level 1 controlled state so the player sees the map layer and response decisions right away. The national spirit gives a small daily communist drift, and each communist-controlled state adds +0.01 daily communist support through dynamic pressure. States progress through Agitation Zone, Insurgent Stronghold, and Communist Lockdown levels; Level 3 creates a demilitarized revolutionary lockdown zone. Local military intervention works only on Levels 1-2; Disrupt Communist Organizing reduces national communist support; emergency national intervention affects all controlled states and can trigger a custom rebel country without vanilla stockpile splitting. Once controlled states are gone, rebels are not active, and communist support falls below the spread threshold. World Revolution stays locked until Whispers of the World Revolution is reached.
Evo I: Gathering Storm: Unstable Revolutionary Activity begins once any state is communist-controlled. Enables rare surprise revolts, including very rare one-state breakaway revolts with rebel armies scaled by state and country strength.
Evo II: Rising Chaos: Dark Worker Rituals begins once a Level 2 stronghold exists. Enables rare worker ritual incidents that disrupt a controlled state, raise intervention risk, improve later conversion chance, and slightly increase communist support.
Evo III: Chaos Tier: Whispers of the World Revolution begins once a Level 3 lockdown exists. Unlocks World Revolution for the major-event pool. Later whisper events add 200 World Revolution weight and mark states as more likely to join uprisings.
World-End Scenario: No terminal world-end. Whispers of the World Revolution hands the communist crisis to the separate World Revolution major event, where controlled states may become revolutionary bases.

Details:
The outbreak begins in one random populous state. Zombies use only manpower for their divisions, and thus depend a lot on the population of states they capture. If the horde gets momentum, it spreads fast and captured land is cored right away.

Secondary outbreaks happen most likely in big, crowded, less developed states. Chaos makes those outbreaks more common over time, and each zombie evolution makes the horde harder to contain.

If you want to keep the event under control, the main things that matter are holding the front, cutting outbreak risk with prevention decisions, pushing cure research, and joining the Anti-Zombie League.
Evo I: Gathering Storm: the first major zombie adaptation makes the horde much harder to starve out and much stronger at night. It is the point where early containment starts slipping, and cure work begins getting harder.
Evo II: Rising Chaos: the horde turns into a faster assault force with better attack pressure and even less reliance on supply. Finding the cure becomes harder again.
Evo III: Chaos Tier: weak fronts can collapse fast, and the cure is at its hardest to finish.
World-End Scenario:
Zombie Apocalypse

The outbreak has outgrown every line built to contain it. The dead move from ruined cities into the last organized refuges, while the living lose the roads, laboratories, and armies needed to answer them.

The Zombie Horde becomes the dominant order of the world. Isolated survivors remain in scattered refuges under a world ordered by the dead.

Details: Transforms Tibet or a Tibet-centered Himalayan state into the Holy Realm. The route begins as a defensive mountain refuge, develops into a Bodhisattva-led state, creates the Arhat Administration, reaches the Buddha Mandate, and can branch into restraint, peacekeeping, coercive pacification, Divine Sovereignty, or the final doctrine. Evolutions are focus-path gates; the actual mechanics come from the selected focuses, decisions, and events inside those unlocked paths.
Evo I: Mountain Refuge: forms The Holy Realm, initializes Mandala and Buddhahood counters, applies fragile refuge ideas, opens the Mandala GUI/category, loads the focus tree, and starts shelter, road, refugee, early teaching, and defensive play.
Evo II: Bodhisattva Teaching and Meditation: Send Dhamma Envoys, Guard the Pilgrimage Route, Translate the Wheel, teaching-under-fire, and the concentration-vow sequence raise Bodhi, Compassion, Dhyana Depth, and Meditation Charge while tracking clean-route and Defilement risks.
Evo III: Governance, Sanctuary, Guardian, and Sangha Compact routes: Council/Regent/Assembly choices, infrastructure and supply works, Temple Guard and pilgrimage escort systems, compact admission, aid, anti-puppet clauses, and AI weights support defensive humanitarian play against special chaos countries.
Evo IV: The Unshaken Seat and Powers: Buddhahood requires 108 Bodhi, Fourth Dhyana, low Defilements, teaching successes, crisis teaching, and the focus marker. Success changes leader/stage, fires The Awakened One, unlocks the Buddha powers category, and the first anti-chaos power display fires Powers of the Awakened.
Evo V: Final Silence and Schism: the hidden False Buddha branch supports debate, exile, suppression, and absorption outcomes. Extinction of Defilements, Witnesses Gather, and the final doctrine balance gate non-terminal Empty Seat aftermath versus terminal Final Silence.
World-End Scenario:
The Final Silence

The Holy Realm carries its last doctrine into firing tables, distant commands, and the machinery of war. Its arsenals serve a single purpose: silence.

The Empty Seat's final order silences organized resistance and ordinary state life. Radio networks, armies, and governments disappear into a world that has fallen quiet.

Details: A random eligible country declares war on another eligible country. Higher chaos stages create larger linked war webs. Compatible special countries can appear in later stages.
Evo I: Gathering Storm: Triangular Incident. Three declarations fire in one linked dispute.
Evo II: Rising Chaos: Four Fronts. Four declarations fire in one conflict web, with a small chance for a compatible special country to appear.
Evo III: Chaos Tier: Contagious Ultimatums. Five declarations fire, major countries and faction members become more likely, and special-country involvement becomes more common.
Evo IV: Totalen Chaos: The War Week. Six declarations fire in a short chain, with a strong chance of one compatible special country participating.
Evo V: World Collapse: Open Season. Seven to eight declarations fire while normal random events still run. Compatible special countries are strongly favored when available.

Details:
The Soviet Union is losing command over its republics, rail offices, garrisons, and depots. Moscow can answer with force, negotiation, isolation, or party discipline, but each visible failure gives local authorities more room to act.

Forced-labor quotas, grain extraction, and NKVD campaigns can briefly reinforce Moscow's authority, but each use deepens famine pressure, republic fear, old-movement grievance, and the evidence record. Once the crisis becomes severe, repression can no longer reduce the terminal threat.

Breakaway republics can seek recognition, seize depots, coordinate defenses, or draw more republics into the crisis while Moscow tries to restore command or force a new settlement.
Evo I: First Durable Secession: a republic ministry, garrison, or depot network stops obeying Moscow and survives long enough to make its break visible.
Evo II: Regional Cascade: several republics are free, and release pressure spreads through foreign attention, depot weakness, League coordination, and public refusal.
Evo III: Union Unmade: Moscow has lost Union-wide command. Remaining ordinary republics are forced out of the old center, and the former Union enters open war over its borders.
Evo IV: Maximum Rupture: every remaining republic and eligible special splinter can break from the former Union. The crisis becomes a map-wide struggle over who inherits the old state.
Evo V: World Collapse Rupture: the same break reaches its final intensity, forcing the last eligible remnants into the open while the former Union becomes one front among a collapsing world.

Details:
Across several regions, provisional states rise together from local claims, prepared institutions, regional identities, and remembered polities. Former hosts retain a remnant while the new governments face unsettled borders, disputed assets, fragile forces, and urgent questions of recognition, government, security, and patronage.

Evo I:
The Manuals Cross the Border

Founding charters, civil-service manuals, recognition protocols, and trusted couriers now pass from one young state to the next. New governments enter the world with stronger institutions, earlier diplomatic contacts, and a network prepared to sponsor their survival.
Evo II:
Old Nations Wake

Dormant national projects and half-remembered unions return to political life. Regional and signature independence movements can surface sooner, while the states already born from the wave gain the confidence and institutions needed to rediscover larger identities.
Evo III:
Flags Rise Behind the Barracks

The next declarations arrive with officers, guarded depots, and plans for immediate defense. Breakaway governments gain stronger military budgets and better prepared forces, but every rifle issued sharpens instability, former-host hostility, and the fear of reconquest.
Evo IV:
The Sovereigns Take Their Seats

The informal network becomes a congress of delegates, observers, and rejected clients. Recognition missions, arbitration, rescue commitments, and a shared reserve draw the independent states toward collective leadership without deciding the charter they must ultimately choose.
Evo V:
No Border Is Final

World collapse strips old borders of their final authority. New sovereignty projects enter the struggle for independence, while existing breakaways gain the freedom and pressure to pursue dangerous routes.

Details: Fury turns an eligible non-player minor country into an expansionist war state while keeping the player, subjects, majors, player-linked countries, and island-only countries out of the selection pool. The actor receives the Fury Column template, stockpiles scaled to its size, recurring reinforcement waves, War Office decisions, and a shared focus tree. Fury seeks valid neighboring targets, records its first conquest, and escalates through Hardened Fury, second-actor cooperation or rivalry, all-border pressure, and world-end containment.
Evo I: Hardened Fury: unlocks once the first Fury cycle escalates. Future and eligible current Fury actors receive the hardened national spirit, more starting columns, higher momentum, and a stronger sustained reinforcement profile.
Evo II: Second War Table: ensures at least two Fury actors can exist, unlocks cooperation and rivalry content, enables Fury Pact handling, and records the second evolution in the event log.
Evo III: All Borders Burn: ensures up to three Fury actors, strengthens weekly growth, allows all-border declarations, and unlocks the world-end candidate focus path.
World-End Scenario:
The World in Fury

Fury is no longer confined to one rogue state. Armed hosts answer one another across continents, each treating the nearest border as an invitation to attack and every pause as weakness.

A network of Fury states opens a global war without a negotiated political end. Rage becomes the world's governing order.

Details: Public accusations, leaked cables, and military bulletins unsettle foreign offices before any government admits that a crisis exists. In calmer periods the alarm chiefly raises international tension. As chaos deepens, repeated incidents poison relations, quicken the rhythm of later crises, push governments toward readiness, and may turn a disputed frontier into a limited clash.
Evo I: Cable Traffic Increase. Cable traffic swells as embassies answer rumours with denials. Relations begin to fray, and each new dispatch makes the next alarm easier to believe.
Evo II: Competing Accusations. Competing accusations spread through more capitals. Delayed reports keep old suspicions alive, while cautious governments quietly raise their readiness.
Evo III: Staff Readiness. General staffs begin treating rumour as warning. Diplomatic shocks linger, frontier incidents become harder to contain, and peaceful governments watch the Thin Wire with growing unease.
Evo IV: Extended Alert. Extended alert becomes the normal condition. Heavier accusations and exhausted border commands make a limited frontier clash more likely, even while every government insists that peace still holds.

Details:
White Peace searches for wars that can end without conquest, indemnity, or scripted-story damage. At first it settles one minor country pair under the same flags and the same borders.

Later evolutions can settle several minor pairs, rarely include a major country, or issue broader diplomatic settlements when the world has too many wars.

Its selection weight rises with active wars and valid minor-war candidates, but repeated firings and higher evolutions keep it from becoming common.
Evo I: Repeated Minor Settlements: Repeated Minor Settlements lets one firing quiet several minor fronts when enough safe pairs exist.
Evo II: Major-Country Settlement: Major-Country Settlement allows a rare no-gain exit involving a major country when the war segment can be settled without rewriting the wider conflict.
Evo III: Broad Diplomatic Settlement: Broad Diplomatic Settlement lets one armistice circular quiet broader safe war clutter while leaving protected wars untouched.

Details:
Death is a hidden island crisis that can become a war. It begins by taking one remote island and waiting in silence. Before the public reveal, island spread looks for small island states, especially nearby islands under 100K people, before widening to other low-population island targets.

When Death consumes a state, the state is not occupied in the normal way. Its full population is removed and recorded in the Deaths System, then the state is transferred to Death, cored by Death, stripped of factories, dockyards, ports, infrastructure, and other usable buildings, and marked with the active wasteland modifier. Local manpower, factories, resources, supply, and movement are ruined there. Units caught inside are withered, and recaptured wastelands stay dangerous until countries invest in recovery work.

Death grows through the Black Ledger. Each consumed state adds soul power, and consumed population adds more at one soul power per 250K people. After the world-end stage begins, last-shore footholds add extra soul power as well. Available soul power is what Death has generated but not yet spent.

Death spends soul power on forced island spread, mainland pressure, and ghost hosts. Early hosts are weak and passive, later hosts become stronger, and the world-end stage lets Death open last-shore footholds on surviving continents.

Living countries answer through investigation decisions, early survey boats, war declarations after the danger is clearer, coastal watches, quarantine lines, the Living Compact, wasteland entry gear, dead-zone outposts, and risky Black Book methods. Defeating Death means retaking every state it controls.
Evo I: Second Shore: Death can unlock its first island-spread focus path. It can begin taking more low-population islands, but the pace remains slow and the mainland route stays closed.
Evo II: Mainland Hunger: Death can press the island pattern faster and unlock the mainland focus path. A valid coastal mainland state can become the public reveal point once enough island pressure exists.
Evo III: First Hosts: Near the 600 chaos mark, Death can gain weak custom ghost divisions with very low organization. They hold borders passively and are much weaker than infantry.
Evo IV: Hollow Hosts: Near the 800 chaos mark, Death can gain more custom ghost divisions with higher organization and strength. They remain weaker than infantry and should still be pushable.
Evo V: World End: Once Death has consumed a full continent and Chaos is above 1000, Death gains many infantry-parity hosts and begins attacking aggressively.
World-End Scenario:
Last Shores

Death has emptied enough land to turn islands, wastelands, and ghost hosts into one design. A consumed continent gives Zol the ground from which to reach every surviving shore.

New footholds open across the living world, and the dead march from the last shores to complete the Black Ledger. No population remains beyond Death's count.

Details: Strangers keep meeting in the wrong places. Couriers vanish, equipment fails, and the same quiet methods turn up in distant incidents. Following the trail can expose the pattern, and a few sensible precautions may blunt whatever comes next.
Evo I:
Repeating Methods

The same routes, tricks, and timings are turning up far beyond the first incidents. Leaks and defections reveal pieces of the connection, even if the full list of partners stays hidden.
Evo II:
Coordinated Interference

The incidents now point to an organized foreign campaign. Covert attacks are growing bolder, and the country must decide whom to suspect, which sources to trust, and how much to prepare.
Evo III:
Approaching Confrontation

Border pressure, military precautions, and nervous public warnings are piling up. The hidden crisis is close to becoming an open confrontation, but the opening moves can still be changed.

Details: An African government has started pulling the continent together with aid, guarantees, liberation deals, and a common Charter. Other countries can join, bargain, walk away, or build a rival camp. If the project keeps its promises, regional congresses and constitutional settlements can turn the idea into roads, armies, laws, and a fierce argument over who carries the cost.
Evo I:
Regional Consolidation

The Charter League has kept its first promise and can finally look beyond one corridor. Regional congresses, negotiated settlements, restoration claims, and rival blocs will decide whether its protection grows into lasting cooperation.
Evo II:
Continental Machinery

The League is settling into daily life. Shared railways, emergency forces, membership law, and resource bargains tie distant councils together, and every new connection brings another bill or obligation.
Evo III:
Africa as a World Pole

Africa's settlement has become a question every great power must answer. Foreign bases, sanctions, continent-wide mobilization, strange new actors, and rival projects are now part of the same struggle.
World-End Scenario:
The World Is One

No baseline world-end branch is certified. The terminal settlement remains gated until every external continent package and rival is resolved, W5 world-initial certification receives its pre-install receipts, and the terminal super-event/audio, unique models, and native-language review are complete.

Details: Rivers burst their banks, faults split open, storms tear through rail lines, ash buries farms, and wildfires outrun the roads. Each disaster leaves a local fight to rescue survivors, steady the region, and rebuild before the next emergency arrives.
Evo I:
Wider Disaster Seasons

Bad seasons bring several disasters close together. Rescue crews, supplies, and safe roads become harder to share when every region seems to need them at once.
Evo II:
Regional Cascades

The damage spills across state lines. Broken transport, hunger, disease, refugees, and exhausted reconstruction crews turn one ruined region into a problem for all its neighbors.
Evo III:
Abnormal Paths

The disasters begin moving in impossible ways. Ruptures, meteors, ash clouds, storms, tornadoes, and tsunamis travel across whole regions, giving countries only a rough idea of where the next blow will land.

Details:
Burial parties vanish from an army at war. Ration books are quietly changed, bodies are cut apart, and frightened soldiers whisper that officers are protecting the people responsible.

The army must feed its units, protect witnesses, and hunt organized killers without turning the whole front into a panic. Covering up the crimes may keep order for a while, but it also gives the predators room to recruit.
Evo I:
Ritualized Ranks

Scattered predators now share oaths, marks, ranks, and protection. The cells recognize one another, though nobody can find a headquarters.
Evo II:
The Organized Network

Cells in different countries use the same ledgers, courier routes, prisoner rules, and attack schedules. The network is clearly organized, but its center is still hidden.
Evo III:
Hannibal Lecter Commands

Hannibal Lecter steps into public view and begins drawing the mature network into one command.
World-End Scenario:
The World Is the Larder

Lecter's host has pulled the feeding territories and armed kitchens into one command. Roads, farms, prisons, and conquered cities are all treated as parts of the same larder. Surviving countries are reduced to prey, raiders, or small resistance enclaves.

The network has no reason to hide anymore. Every government still standing faces an expanding host that intends to feed on the whole world.

No Thaw Will Come

Lecter's winter host has given itself to the Wendigo hunger. Feeding grounds spread with the cold, and conquered communities are dragged into a world where thaw, harvest, and mercy are treated as weaknesses.

Winter advances with the host. Every surviving country is hunted until human rule is consumed or driven into a handful of frozen refuges.

Details:
A translated manifesto slips out of reading rooms and into the government of a small country. It promises that common stores, useful work, and public need can build a fairer society. Its readers quickly split over who gets to decide what people need and how much freedom the plan can afford.

Shortages, public works, local charters, and deals with neighboring states put every promise to the test. The commonwealth must prove that it can care for people without turning necessity into an excuse for control or conquest.
Evo I:
Glosses in the Margin

Everyone has started writing in the manifesto's margins. Workers, parishes, councils, families, and exiles bring their own copies and their own answers. The movement's future may belong to whoever keeps the right to edit the book.
Evo II:
Necessary Shores

Migration, blockades, crowded homes, and thin supplies push the common store to its limits. Surveyors search for harbors, corridors, settlements, and leases that can meet real needs without turning the commonwealth into a hungry neighbor.
Evo III:
Cities of One Measure

The plan has escaped the capital. Towns and rebuilt districts are opening gardens, clinics, workshops, stores, and transport links of their own. Local votes and local shortages shape each version, and arguments over work reveal who really gets to change the plan.
Evo IV:
Nowhere Made Law

The manifesto now has a place in regional politics. Governments quote it when they ask for aid, defend local charters, refuse threats, or seek association. Small states must decide whether the commonwealth looks like a refuge, a useful partner, or an ambitious neighbor.
Evo V:
The Perfect Island

The world around the commonwealth is coming apart. Reserve trains, guarded harbors, refugee districts, fortifications, and member councils all compete for the same supplies. One path closes the gates and demands service from everyone inside. The other shares refuge among willing towns and spreads the burden across the league.

Details:
Doctor Warren Kruger arrives with working results in fields that rarely fit inside one career, much less one mind. A government can hire him openly, hide him inside a Directorate, or point his talents somewhere else. Wherever he settles, universities, factories, armies, and foreign spies gather around the same guarded rooms.

Kruger's laboratory soon becomes an institution with secrets and ambitions of its own. Everyone accepts that he is brilliant. The government must still prove it can command what his brilliance creates.
Evo I:
National Scientific Ascendancy

Kruger's laboratory has become part of national life. His methods are spreading through universities, factories, hospitals, and military planning.
Evo II:
The International Scientific Contest

Foreign governments are courting Kruger, copying his work, and sending people to steal it. The scientific race is becoming a struggle between states.
Evo III:
Forbidden and Autonomous Science

The Directorate is repeating experiments that ordinary ministries can barely understand, much less supervise. Every dangerous success draws more people and facilities into Kruger's private network.
Evo IV:
Sovereign Science

Kruger has stopped asking permission. He arrives with a demand for political authority and the backing of laboratories, staff, and machines that answer to him.
World-End Scenario:
Laboratory World

Kruger's Directorate has swallowed the governments that once tried to supervise it. Countries, populations, and whole landscapes survive as controlled samples inside a planetary laboratory.

The world has become one experiment, and Kruger alone decides what happens to the control group.

The Strategic Singularity

The Directorate's final device tears through armies, cities, and the air itself. The blast leaves mass death, poisoned ground, and governments too broken to hold the old world together.

The Singularity ends Kruger's experiment and leaves the survivors in a world of fallout.

Details:
A small neutral country is running out of room to stand alone. The great blocs offer protection, weapons, and a seat at their table, then make it clear that refusing everyone may be the most dangerous choice.

The winning faction will worry nearby neutrals and send its envoys toward the next exposed border. Neutrality becomes something a country must defend with speeches, councils, troops, and a fair bit of nerve.
Evo I:
Regional Bloc Race

One accession starts a regional scramble. Border guards dig in, observers arrive, neutrality councils meet, and faction officers make themselves comfortable in nearby capitals.
Evo II:
Pressured Neutrality

War makes neutrality harder to sell. Countries beside active fronts receive sharper demands, louder promises, and less time to answer.
Evo III:
Collapse of Neutrality

Several small states can be pulled toward rival blocs in quick succession. The last neutral capitals answer with hurried councils, guarded borders, and expensive promises to stand alone.

Details: Surveyors have struck a major deposit in one of the country's states. The first find promises jobs, trade, and new industry. Repeated discoveries can turn the same field into a boomtown, a diplomatic prize, or something much harder to control.
Evo I:
Veins Without End

One field keeps giving. New deposits appear beneath old workings, and foreign buyers, rival claimants, and would-be peacekeepers all want a share of the wealth.
Evo II:
The Workings Turn Sick

Miners fall sick, metal corrodes overnight, people vanish, and something attacks in the lower workings. The country must investigate, contain the danger, or close the field before the boomtown becomes a grave.
Evo III:
The Breach Takes Shape

A huge mixed deposit pulls the workings far below safe ground. Attacks reach the surface, and the country must hunt what escaped, evacuate the field, or seal away every valuable shaft before the breach fully opens.
Evo IV:
The Oth-Kesh Emerge

The field opens into an Oth-Kesh origin chamber. Armored broods pour through the workings, feed on rich deposits, and attack every country they can reach as they search for roads beneath the next continent.
World-End Scenario:
The World Opens Below

The Oth-Kesh have secured their first continent and opened new chambers beyond the sea. The tunnels below become roads for armored broods, and fresh fronts tear open beneath the richest ground.

Every surviving continent now has its own entrance to the World Below. The surface is caught in one global war against the depths.

Details:
Fully formed military units are appearing across the world with no recruitment orders, training records, or known home. Governments suddenly have to feed, equip, command, and watch soldiers who arrived ready to march.

Some formations bring strange weapons, ambitious commanders, or troops that are not human at all. A useful windfall can become a rival army very quickly.
Evo I:
Organized Muster

The soldiers from nowhere now have district staffs, proper rolls, and officers the government can actually hold responsible.
Evo II:
Arsenal Lottery

New formations arrive carrying baffling mixes of weapons and gear. Each one needs its own training, spare parts, and supply plan.
Evo III:
Command Fracture

Some new commanders inspire more loyalty than the government that received them. Their private authority can split an army or put a claimant in the capital.
Evo IV:
Anomalous Muster

Not every arriving host is human. Governments must decide whether to quarter these soldiers, bargain with them, or turn them away before an armed camp becomes a country of its own.

Details:
A black-marked fever has broken out on the mainland. It moves through roads, ports, hungry cities, and rat-filled ruins, leaving governments to choose which places to isolate and which people they can still save.

If the plague is allowed to settle in, the rats may become something more dangerous than carriers. Whole warrens can learn to fight, govern, and follow a king of their own.
Evo I:
The Strain Grows Stronger

The plague has learned to thrive in crowded and poorly protected places. Deaths rise faster, and every untreated corridor helps the next wave spread.
Evo II:
The Plague Crosses the Sea

Ports and long-distance transport carry the plague beyond its mainland cradle. Docks, troop convoys, refugees, and wartime shipping can open a second front across the sea.
Evo III:
The Warrens Raise Flags

Collapsed plague basins have joined the reusable RTA Rat Nation carrier. Its broods seize infected ground and build armies without human soldiers or ordinary equipment.
Evo IV:
The Rat King Wakes

A royal basin has learned to obey one sentient ruler. The separate RTX Rat King gathers memory, hunger, and authority as the surviving broods decide whether to kneel.
Evo V:
The Kingdom of Teeth

The Rat King's dominion has grown beyond the warrens. Capitals fall silent, refuges are overrun, and the last continental cordons begin to break.
World-End Scenario:
The Kingdom of Teeth

The Black Plague has crossed the final threshold. The sentient Rat King has completed its royal route, seized the required capitals and refuge nodes, and brought an eligible continent under one crown. Evolution V begins the deterministic takeover: human administrations collapse, the rat dominion claims the surviving infrastructure, and the world enters a new order ruled from the Royal Basin.
